title: Setting the Load Down
logline: Estate workers carry tea-leaf baskets down a mountain path all morning, and the moment each basket reaches the weighing shed and comes off a back, something visibly changes in the body underneath it.

object.note: Object 6 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: A mother's care leads to the bodies of those who carry: tea-leaf baskets coming off backs at the weighing shed, and relief visible in the body underneath.

thread_out.thread: Relief in a working body gives way to bodies that can no longer carry much: carers at an elders' home moving within one hour from a frightened moment to good news.

requirements: An active tea estate willing to allow filming of real pickers over a working day
Honest access to conditions and pay, not only the picturesque parts of the process
Workers' full consent to be filmed and interviewed

lesson.in_simple_terms: The texts describe a good mind as a lighter one, and their picture for that lightness is someone setting down a heavy load they have carried a long way. Kindness, in this account, comes with a kind of relief.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: දුර සිට ඔසවාගෙන ආ බරක් බිම තැබූ විට දැනෙන සැහැල්ලුව මෙන්, යහපත් සිතකත් සැහැල්ලු බවක් හා සහනයක් ඇති බව අභිධර්මය උගන්වයි.
lesson.the_teaching: Among the nineteen beautiful factors present in every good mind are paired qualities of tranquillity and lightness. Lightness opposes the heaviness of sloth and torpor, which the Pradeepika says is not the weight of any substance but the mind's dullness, and its image is putting down a burden carried from far away; tranquillity opposes restlessness, like someone scorched by the sun reaching the shade of a tree. In these pairs the word 'body' refers to the group of accompanying mental factors, not the physical body. The texts also teach that effort itself is neither good nor bad, taking the quality of the mind it joins.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The film follows baskets going up the slope empty at dawn, the weight accumulating through the morning, the walk down, and the weighing. It holds without comment on the exact moment each basket comes off a back, in the shoulders and the breathing, and lets that outward relief stand as a picture of an inward quality the narration never names.

key_terms.en: the group of accompanying mental factors, not the physical body

lesson.caution: This does not mean goodness is simply feeling light or feeling good; the texts also say that turning the mind toward the good takes effort against a natural pull the other way.
lesson.builds_on: The mother's care changed shape for each child; this film turns to what every good moment shares, the ease and lightness that come with it, seen in the bodies of those who carry.
